ut_lower_tier.blurb: The Lower Tier is the second terrace of the Graveside Matter Wall in Cedar Canyon, up the highway from Cedar City. It is mainly a sport crag: sixteen bolted lines on steep, featured sandstone, plus one trad line and one aid line. Grades start in the 5.8 range and build toward the top end, with the bulk of the climbing between 5.10 and 5.12 and a single route above that. Expect a good draw for climbers who have moved past moderates. The wall catches morning shade and then afternoon sun, and the surrounding canyon is wooded, so it is a pleasant place for a day out.
ut_lower_tier.approach: From the main pullout, follow the established path up the canyon past a large boulder, then take a switchback to the left that leads up to the base of the wall.

ut_drone_wall.blurb: Drone Wall is a single mushroom-shaped outcrop tucked among trees beside a stream in the right fork of Hobble Creek Canyon, east of Springville. All eighteen routes here are bolted. The spread is wide for such a small crag: a handful of easy and moderate lines in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, a couple of 5.10s, and a strong block of 5.11s, topped by a 5.12 and a 5.13. The rock is pocketed and sharp, so expect rough texture on the fingers. The cliff is out of sight of the road, and it works as a quick local sport stop rather than a big destination.

ut_alley_the.blurb: The Alley is a sport crag within the Sunset Alley zone off Beaver Dam Road, west of St. George, at roughly 5,000 feet. It holds eighteen bolted routes with a mix of overhanging, slab and vertical terrain, and most of the climbing is fairly technical. Grades run from one easy 5.8 through a solid band of 5.10s, then a few 5.11s and a good number of 5.12s, with a couple of 5.13s at the top. That makes it best suited to climbers comfortable on harder sport. The wall goes into shade from about early afternoon, which helps on warm days.

ut_pa_s_mother.blurb: PA's Mother is a small face in Rock Canyon above Provo, on the north side of the creek just where the canyon tightens. Eighteen routes split between bolted sport and trad, with a handful of top-rope options. The grade range is broad, from a scrambly 5.3 or so up to a 5.12, with a good amount in the 5.6 to 5.10 zone, so it suits mixed parties and newer leaders. The rock is quartzite. Most lines are short, and all can be descended by rappel or by walking off. The base is reached on a short trail across talus, which is gentler than the old direct scramble.
ut_pa_s_mother.approach: Past the second canyon gate, cross the creek on logs near the concrete structures. Follow the trail north toward The Appendage, then continue east on the newer trail over talus to the base of the face.

ut_dead_snag_the.blurb: The Dead Snag is a trad wall on the south side of Big Cottonwood Canyon, a short walk from the Storm Mountain Picnic Area. It has eighteen routes, almost all of them trad, with two bolted lines. Many are long, with several two- and three-pitch outings, and the grades run mainly from 5.5 to 5.10 with one 5.11 at the top end. That makes it a well-regarded spot for people learning to place gear or wanting a relaxed multi-pitch day. The rock is quartzite, which can feel slick and hard. Rappel descents run down the face, so watch for other parties above and below.

ut_santaquin_canyon_ice.blurb: Santaquin Canyon Ice is a winter venue in the southern Wasatch, with twelve ice lines and six mixed climbs. Most flows sit on the shaded south side of the canyon, and a lot of them can be seen from the road. Ice grades centre on WI4, with a few easier and several harder lines up to the WI6 range, while the mixed routes cover a wide band from moderate M-grades into double digits. Many climbs are one or two pitches, and the lines tend to run in gullies that can slide, so avalanche conditions matter a great deal. Snowmobile traffic and weekend crowds are common.

ut_cerberus_gendarme.blurb: Cerberus Gendarme is a sandstone buttress on the east side of Zion Canyon, directly across the river from Moonlight Buttress. It is a trad-focused wall with eighteen routes, mostly crack climbs, and a good number of them are multi-pitch. Most lines fall in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a few easier options near 5.7 and 5.8 and a couple of 5.12 and 5.13 lines. The main draw is a long, classic big-wall route, and the rest of the formation offers shorter free climbs. Zion sandstone is fragile when wet, so avoid it during and after rain. The walk from the road to the base is brief.

ut_shady_corridor.blurb: Shady Corridor is the first sector you meet on entering Lambs Knoll, a compact cluster of sandstone crags near Virgin and Zion. It has eighteen routes, mostly sport, with some trad and two top-rope lines. Nearly half the climbing sits at 5.10, with a scattering of easier lines from 5.6 to 5.9 and one 5.11. As the name suggests, many climbs here stay shaded for most or all of the day, which makes spring and fall the sweet spots at around 6,000 feet. The sandstone is soft, so let it dry out fully after any rain.
